the video likely encouraged visitors to spend more time with the painting.
questions.explanation: Visitors stayed much longer when the video was added, so the video probably encouraged them to linger. The data do not show that visitors preferred videos to paintings in general, and time spent rose in the second month.

questions.passage: The Svalbard archipelago in the Arctic has no native trees, yet geologists have found coal there, which forms from the remains of plants that once grew in thick forests. Studies of the rocks also show that over hundreds of millions of years, the land that now forms Svalbard has moved slowly across the globe as Earth's crustal plates shifted. Together, these findings suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the land that is now Svalbard was probably once located in a warmer region where forests could grow.
coal can form from plants that grow in very cold climates without trees.
the coal on Svalbard was most likely carried there by glaciers from elsewhere.
Svalbard's climate will soon become warm enough for forests to return.
questions.explanation: Coal requires former forests, and the land has moved across the globe, so the likeliest explanation is that it once sat in a warmer place where forests grew. The text gives no evidence for glaciers carrying coal or for a future change.

questions.passage: Researchers studying a population of songbirds noticed that birds living near a busy highway sang at a higher pitch than birds of the same species living in a quiet forest nearby. Traffic noise is mostly low-pitched. When the researchers played recordings of traffic in the forest, the forest birds also began singing at a higher pitch within a few days. These results suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the highway birds and forest birds belong to different species.
birds near highways sing higher because they are smaller than forest birds.
the birds may raise the pitch of their songs so that their songs are not drowned out by low-pitched noise.
traffic noise causes birds to stop singing entirely.
questions.explanation: Low-pitched noise and higher-pitched songs, plus forest birds shifting upward when traffic sounds were played, suggest the birds adjust to be heard over the noise. The text says the birds are the same species and does not mention size.

questions.passage: Researchers studying a lake found that the number of a small fish species dropped sharply in the years after a larger predatory fish was introduced. During the same years, the number of tiny water insects that the small fish eat increased greatly. Based on these observations, the researchers suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the predatory fish reduced the small fish population, which allowed the insects that small fish eat to multiply.
the water insects were eating the small fish.
the predatory fish ate mostly water insects.
the small fish moved to another lake to find more insects.
questions.explanation: Fewer small fish (eaten by the predator) means less pressure on the insects they eat, so the insects increased. Nothing suggests insects eat fish, that the predator eats insects, or that the small fish moved.

questions.passage: Chemist Elena Varga found that a newly developed paint dries quickly on sunny days but stays wet for hours on cloudy days, even when the temperature and humidity are the same on both kinds of days. In the laboratory, the paint dried quickly under an ultraviolet lamp but slowly under an ordinary lamp that produced the same amount of heat. Varga concludes that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the paint dries quickly only when the air is very dry.
ordinary lamps produce more ultraviolet light than sunlight does.
the paint dries faster when the temperature is higher.
ultraviolet light, rather than heat, is likely what speeds up the drying of the paint.
questions.explanation: Drying speed changed with ultraviolet light while heat, temperature and humidity were held equal, so ultraviolet light is the likely cause. Temperature and humidity were the same, so choices A and C are not supported.

questions.passage: Two friends planted sunflower seeds from the same packet on the same day. One watered her seeds every day, while the other watered his only once a week. After a month, the sunflowers that were watered daily were twice as tall. This suggests that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: sunflowers grow best in shade.
the seeds came from two different packets.
watering does not affect sunflower growth.
more frequent watering likely helped the sunflowers grow taller.
questions.explanation: The seeds and planting day were the same, and only the watering differed, so watering is the likely reason for the height difference. The text says the seeds came from the same packet.

questions.passage: An airline noticed that passengers complained much less about long waits at the baggage claim after the company moved arrival gates farther from the baggage area. Passengers now spent most of the waiting time walking instead of standing still, even though the total time from leaving the plane to receiving bags did not change. This suggests that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: passengers may mind a wait less when they are kept busy than when they stand idle.
passengers prefer airports with fewer gates.
bags arrived faster after the gates were moved.
walking long distances makes passengers more likely to complain.
questions.explanation: The total wait stayed the same, but complaints fell when passengers spent the time walking instead of standing. That suggests an active wait feels shorter. The text says bags did not arrive faster.

questions.passage: Many coastal birds build their nests on the ground. On one island, researchers found that a species of tern nested mostly on bare sand in years when rats were absent, but nested mostly on rocky cliffs in years after rats were accidentally introduced. Rats eat eggs but cannot easily climb the island's steep cliffs. The researchers also found that chicks raised on cliffs grew more slowly, because the parents had to fly farther to find food. These findings suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: terns prefer cliffs to sand when no predators are present.
the rats were introduced because the terns moved to the cliffs.
chicks raised on the cliffs were safer from food shortages than chicks raised on sand.
the terns' shift to cliffs likely protected their eggs from rats but came at a cost to chick growth.
questions.explanation: The terns moved to cliffs when rats arrived, and rats cannot climb the cliffs, but cliff chicks grew more slowly. So the move traded safety from rats for slower growth. Without rats, terns chose sand, so they do not prefer cliffs.

questions.passage: In a study of reading habits, people who read printed books before bed reported falling asleep faster than people who read on bright tablet screens. However, when the researchers asked tablet readers to switch on a setting that dims the screen and removes blue light, the difference in time to fall asleep largely disappeared. These results suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: reading itself makes it harder to fall asleep.
the light from bright screens, rather than reading on a tablet as such, may delay sleep.
printed books contain more interesting stories than tablets.
people who read before bed sleep worse than people who do not read.
questions.explanation: When the tablet's bright blue light was removed, tablet readers fell asleep about as fast as book readers, so the light, not the tablet reading itself, was likely the problem. The study did not compare readers with nonreaders.

questions.passage: In many cities, pigeons gather in large flocks near train stations and town squares, where people often drop food. Researchers in one city found that when a nearby food market closed permanently, the number of pigeons in the surrounding square fell by more than half within a year, even though the square itself did not change. This finding suggests that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: pigeons prefer squares to train stations.
the number of pigeons in an area may depend heavily on how much food people leave there.
the market owners were trying to scare the pigeons away.
pigeons are unable to find food on their own.
questions.explanation: The square stayed the same, but pigeon numbers fell after the food source closed, which suggests food from people strongly affects pigeon numbers. Nothing shows pigeons cannot find food on their own.

questions.passage: Glaciologists drilled into an ice sheet and found a thin layer of fine ash about 300 meters below the surface. By counting the yearly layers of snow above it, they dated the ash to about 1,100 years ago. Historical records from the region describe no volcanic eruption at that time, but a volcano on a distant island is known from geological studies to have erupted violently around then. The glaciologists therefore suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the ash was produced by a forest fire near the ice sheet.
the historical records are wrong about the region's weather.
ash from the distant volcano may have traveled through the atmosphere and fallen onto the ice sheet.
no eruptions occurred anywhere in the world 1,100 years ago.
questions.explanation: No local eruption was recorded, but a distant volcano erupted at the right time, so its ash likely traveled to the ice. Nothing points to a fire or to errors about the weather.

questions.passage: A biology class placed two identical plants on the same windowsill. One plant was given water mixed with fertilizer, and the other was given plain water. After a month, the plant given fertilizer had grown twice as many leaves. The class concluded that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: plants grow only on windowsills.
plain water harms plants.
the fertilizer likely helped the plant grow more leaves.
the plants received different amounts of sunlight.
questions.explanation: The only difference between the plants was the fertilizer, so it likely caused the extra leaves. The plants were on the same windowsill, so they got the same sunlight.

questions.passage: A city gave every household a free kitchen bin for food scraps and began collecting the scraps weekly for composting. Over the next year, the weight of trash sent to the city's landfill fell by 20%, even though the population grew slightly. The city's officials concluded that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: residents were producing less food than before.
much of what had been sent to the landfill was likely food waste that was now being composted instead.
the landfill had been closed for part of the year.
residents stopped using the new bins after a few weeks.
questions.explanation: Landfill trash fell after the food-scrap program began, even with more people, which suggests food waste was being composted instead. If residents had stopped using the bins, trash would not have fallen.

questions.passage: In a study of a mountain stream, researchers found that trout were abundant in sections shaded by trees but rare in nearby sections where the trees had been cleared for farming. Water in the shaded sections stayed below 18°C all summer, while water in the cleared sections often rose above 22°C. Laboratory studies show that this species of trout becomes stressed and stops feeding in water warmer than 20°C. These findings suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: removing the trees likely made the water too warm for the trout, reducing their numbers in those sections.
trout prefer to live near farms.
the trees provided the trout with most of their food.
the farming introduced a predator that ate the trout.
questions.explanation: The cleared sections were warmer than trout can tolerate, while shaded sections stayed cool, so tree removal likely reduced trout through warmer water. Nothing mentions food from trees or a predator.

questions.passage: Historians studying a set of letters written by a nineteenth-century merchant noticed that his handwriting became much shakier in letters dated after 1851. During the same period, the letters' spelling and grammar remained perfect, and their content showed that he was still running his business successfully and negotiating complex contracts. The historians suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: someone else began writing the merchant's letters after 1851.
the merchant's business failed after 1851.
the merchant may have developed a physical condition affecting his hands while his mental abilities remained sharp.
the merchant forgot how to spell after 1851.
questions.explanation: The handwriting worsened but the spelling, grammar and business skill stayed strong, suggesting a physical problem with his hands rather than a mental decline. The business was still successful, and his spelling stayed perfect.

questions.passage: Researchers placed identical feeding stations in two parks. One park had many tall trees; the other had only open grass. Small birds visited the station in the park with trees far more often. When the researchers set up a few artificial shrubs around the station in the open park, visits there increased sharply. These results suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: small birds prefer open grass to trees.
the food at the station in the open park was of lower quality.
small birds may visit feeders more often when there is nearby cover where they can hide from predators.
tall trees produce food that birds prefer over feeder seeds.
questions.explanation: Adding shrubs near the open-park feeder increased visits, which suggests cover matters to the birds. The stations were identical, so food quality was not the difference.

questions.passage: Linguists studying a language found that its oldest written records, from about 800 years ago, contain dozens of words related to sailing and fishing. Records from the same period contain very few words for farming tools, and most farming words that appear today were borrowed from a neighboring language within the last 400 years. Based on this evidence, the linguists suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: speakers of the language never practiced farming.
early speakers of the language may have relied more on the sea than on farming, adopting farming more extensively in later centuries.
the neighboring language has no words related to the sea.
the oldest records of the language were written by visitors from the neighboring region.
questions.explanation: Many early sea-related words and few early farming words, with farming words borrowed later, suggest the early speakers depended on the sea and took up farming more later. "Never" in choice A goes too far.

questions.passage: A school noticed that students were often late to first-period classes. After the school moved the start time thirty minutes later, the number of late students dropped by half, even though bus routes and class lengths stayed the same. The school concluded that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: students preferred longer classes.
the buses had become faster.
the earlier start time was likely a major reason for students being late.
teachers had stopped recording late students.
questions.explanation: The only change was the later start, and lateness dropped, so the early start was probably a big cause. The text says bus routes stayed the same.

questions.passage: A gardener grew the same variety of tomatoes in two greenhouses. Both greenhouses received the same light, water and soil, but one was kept at 24°C and the other at 32°C. The tomatoes in the cooler greenhouse produced far more fruit. The gardener concluded that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: tomatoes need more water at high temperatures.
the soil in the warmer greenhouse was poor.
tomatoes grow best in complete darkness.
very high temperatures may reduce the amount of fruit these tomato plants produce.
questions.explanation: Only temperature differed, and the cooler greenhouse gave more fruit, so high heat likely reduced fruit. The soil and water were the same in both.

questions.passage: Engineers studying an old stone bridge found that its arches had cracked mostly on the downstream side. River records showed that floods had grown more frequent over the past century, and that during floods, debris such as tree trunks piled up against the upstream side of the bridge, pushing it downstream. Laboratory models of the bridge showed that such pressure would bend the arches so that the downstream sides were stretched. The engineers therefore concluded that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the cracks were caused by the bridge's original builders using poor stone.
the cracks most likely formed before the floods became more frequent.
boats striking the downstream side of the bridge caused the cracks.
pressure from flood debris was likely a major cause of the cracking.
questions.explanation: Debris pushes the bridge downstream, models show this stretches the downstream sides, and that is where the cracks are. So flood debris likely caused much of the cracking. Nothing points to poor stone or boats.

questions.passage: In a study of a language-learning app, users who practiced for ten minutes every day for a month learned more vocabulary than users who practiced for seventy minutes once a week, even though both groups practiced for the same total time. Another group that practiced for ten minutes every day but skipped every weekend learned nearly as much as the daily group. These results suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: practicing for longer sessions is the most effective way to learn vocabulary.
frequent, spaced practice sessions may help vocabulary learning more than infrequent long ones.
the total amount of practice time has no effect on learning.
users who skip weekends forget most of what they learned.
questions.explanation: Equal total time produced more learning when spread over frequent short sessions, and skipping weekends cost little. That points to frequent, spaced practice. The study held total time equal, so it cannot show total time has no effect.

questions.passage: The roseate spoonbill and the glossy ibis are long-legged birds that live in wetlands, like the Everglades in Florida. Laura D'Acunto and colleagues wanted to know how these birds choose an area in which to live. They looked at features of these birds' habitats, such as how quickly water drains from the area and the amount of tree-canopy cover there is in the area. They found that roseate spoonbills prefer areas with extensive canopy cover, but this was not true for glossy ibises. The researchers therefore concluded that wetland-management strategies that increase the amount of tree canopy in potential wetland bird habitats are less likely to
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: attract glossy ibises to the area than they are to attract roseate spoonbills to the area.
attract birds that don't typically live in wetlands to the area than they are to attract roseate spoonbills or glossy ibises to the area.
decrease the area's appeal to both roseate spoonbills and glossy ibises than they are to increase the appeal to other species.
extend the average lifespan of roseate spoonbills already in the area than they are to attract a greater number of those birds to the area.
questions.explanation: Spoonbills prefer heavy canopy cover and ibises do not, so adding canopy should draw spoonbills more than ibises. The study says nothing about non-wetland birds, other species or lifespan.

questions.passage: The state of Michigan has classified the balsam woolly adelgid as an invasive species that could outcompete some of the state's native species. But researchers Alejandro Camacho and Jason McLachlan have pointed out that Earth's climate is changing in ways that challenge such classifications. Climate changes may cause animals to alter their current ranges and establish new ones. Climate changes may also create good habitats in areas where a species couldn't live previously. These observations suggest that
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: Michigan may come to find that categorizing the balsam woolly adelgid as invasive no longer reflects environmental reality.
even if Earth's climate doesn't change in the way scientists predict, the balsam woolly adelgid will likely establish itself in Michigan.
Michigan was previously home to some balsam woolly adelgids but they were outcompeted by invading species.
it's useful at present for Michigan to distinguish between invasive and native species in some instances but not in the case of the balsam woolly adelgid.
questions.explanation: If climate change shifts ranges and creates new habitats, a species called "invasive" today may come to belong there naturally. So the label may stop matching reality. Nothing in the text supports B, C or D.

questions.passage: To investigate the root of people's resistance to AI-created art, researchers conducted a study in which participants rated a series of AI-generated artworks that were randomly labeled as "human-created" or "AI-created." Unsurprisingly, participants consistently gave higher scores to those labeled as human-created. One explanation for this is the effort heuristic effect, whereby awareness of the effort invested in a work of art enhances people's appreciation of it. Interestingly, this tendency might also be exploited to mitigate the bias against AI-created art: in another study, participants who had watched videos of robots creating paintings rated the AI-created paintings more favorably than did participants who hadn't watched them, presumably because the videos
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: challenged the assumption that the AI's artistic process involved little to no labor.
allayed anxieties about AI replacing human artists.
acknowledged the influence of human-created art on the AI-created paintings.
attributed a degree of intentionality to the AI.
questions.explanation: The text explains the bias with the **effort heuristic**: visible effort raises appreciation. Videos of robots painting show effort, which challenges the idea that AI art takes no labor. The other choices do not connect to effort.

questions.passage: Like all species of baleen whales, the humpback whale feeds on tiny creatures known as krill by filtering water through bristlelike keratin structures called baleen plates. In this way, baleen whales can eat up to 30 percent of their total mass per day. And while no one would call the humpback whale small—it can have a mass as high as 30,000 kg—it is one of the smaller baleen whales and is much smaller than the fin whale, which can weigh a whopping 80,000 kg and consume as much as 24,000 kg of krill per day.
questions.prompt: Based on the text, what can most reasonably be concluded about krill consumption among humpback and fin whales?
choices: Most baleen whales include krill in their diets, but the humpback whale is less likely than the fin whale to do so.
The fin whale is able to eat more krill per day than the humpback whale is.
Both the humpback whale and the fin whale can eat as much as 24,000 kg of krill per day.
The quantities of krill consumed by fin whales has made it difficult for humpback whales to find sufficient food.
questions.explanation: Both eat up to 30% of their mass. The fin whale is much heavier (80,000 kg against 30,000 kg), so it can eat more: about 24,000 kg, compared with at most 9,000 kg for the humpback.

questions.passage: Honeybees that find a good patch of flowers return to the hive and perform a "waggle dance" for other bees. Researchers suspected that the length of each waggle tells other bees how far away the food is. To test this, they placed one feeder near a hive and another feeder much farther away. Bees returning from the distant feeder performed noticeably longer waggles than bees returning from the nearby feeder. This finding suggests that
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: honeybees prefer to visit feeders that are close to their hive.
the researchers' suspicion about the length of the waggle is likely correct.
the direction of a food source has no effect on the waggle dance.
bees that visit distant feeders collect more food than other bees do.
questions.explanation: Longer distance went with longer waggles, which is what the researchers expected if waggle length signals distance. The study did not test preference (A), direction (C) or amount of food (D).

questions.passage: Blue-footed boobies usually lay two eggs, and parents begin incubating the first egg as soon as it is laid, so the chicks hatch several days apart. Researchers have found that when food is plentiful, the younger chick survives at a rate similar to that of its older sibling. When food is scarce, however, the older chick often outcompetes or even attacks the younger one, which then rarely survives. This pattern suggests that, for the parents, laying a second egg most likely functions as
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: a way to ensure that the first chick receives less food.
a strategy that guarantees two chicks will survive in years when food is scarce.
a cause of food shortages in years when both chicks survive.
a form of insurance that lets the parents raise an additional chick when conditions allow.
questions.explanation: The second chick survives in good years and is lost in bad ones, so it adds a chick only when conditions allow. That is a kind of insurance. Choice B contradicts the text, which says younger chicks rarely survive scarce years.

questions.passage: The Voynich manuscript, a fifteenth-century book written in an unknown script, has resisted every attempt at decipherment. Some scholars have argued that its text is meaningless, an elaborate hoax. Statistical analyses, however, show that the manuscript's "words" follow patterns typical of natural languages: a few words appear very frequently while most appear rarely, and certain words cluster in sections whose illustrations share a subject. Although these findings don't reveal what the text says, they suggest that
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the hoax explanation is less likely than it might otherwise seem.
the manuscript was actually written later than the fifteenth century.
the illustrations were added long after the text was written.
the script is a variant of a known European alphabet.
questions.explanation: Language-like patterns and topic-linked vocabulary are what you would expect from meaningful text, which makes the "meaningless hoax" view less likely. The text says nothing about dating, when the illustrations were added, or which alphabet was used.

questions.passage: Astronomers studying the Sun's quiet regions—areas thought to have little visible activity—recently observed frequent, small gas eruptions. Although individually minor, these eruptions occur nearly constantly. Data from high-resolution satellites revealed that these small eruptions involve magnetic energy release, potentially contributing significantly to the overall heat of the Sun's corona (the outermost layer of its atmosphere). Astronomers are now trying to measure these events more precisely to better understand their role in the Sun's temperature dynamics.
questions.prompt: Based on the text, why do astronomers think that eruptions in the Sun's quiet regions might be important?
choices: Given their frequency, the eruptions could have a substantial cumulative effect on the corona's temperature.
Although they are small, the eruptions are so numerous that they might collectively emit enough gas to alter the corona's composition.
Considering the rate at which they occur, the eruptions may be caused by magnetic energy release.
Despite its small size, any given eruption releases enough magnetic energy to substantially raise the corona's temperature.
questions.explanation: Each eruption is minor, but they happen "nearly constantly," so together they may add significantly to the corona's heat. D contradicts "individually minor"; B is about composition, not heat.

questions.passage: The state of Maine has classified the smallmouth bass as an invasive species that could outcompete some of the state's native fish. But researchers Alejandro Camacho and Jason McLachlan have pointed out that Earth's climate is changing in ways that challenge such classifications. Climate changes may cause animals to leave their current ranges and establish new ones. Climate changes may also create good habitats in areas where a species couldn't live previously. These observations suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: Maine was previously home to some smallmouth bass but they were outcompeted by invading species.
even if Earth's climate doesn't change in the way scientists predict, the smallmouth bass will likely establish itself in Maine.
Maine may come to find that categorizing the smallmouth bass as invasive no longer reflects environmental reality.
it's useful at present for Maine to distinguish between invasive and native species in some instances but not in the case of the smallmouth bass.
questions.explanation: If climate change moves species into new ranges and makes new areas livable, then the smallmouth bass may come to belong in Maine, and the "invasive" label may no longer fit.

questions.passage: In recent years, architects have heightened their focus on developing eco-conscious and sustainable buildings. One way to accomplish this is through biophilic design, which seeks to augment occupants' emotional and physical well-being by establishing a coherent relationship among the building, nature, and human biology. Effective biophilic design is smoothly integrated into its surroundings to harmonize with nature; architects dedicated to this approach therefore typically avoid ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: prioritizing the sustainability of the building materials used in their projects over their personal aesthetic principles.
emphasizing the emotional effects a building's design would have on its occupants.
researching only one location at a time so that each building design incorporates inspiration from as many different natural environments as possible.
designing a new structure without first developing an understanding of its ecological context.

questions.passage: The advent of online streaming has led many music listeners to drift away from ownership of music (through downloads or through physical media such as compact discs) and toward streaming services such as YouTube Music and Jango. Datta et al. studied the impact of this change on the variety of music that listeners consume. The researchers reasoned that the ownership model of music assigns a cost per song to acquiring a variety of music, while streaming services typically charge a flat fee for access to an entire music catalog, making variety free, which suggests that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the music choices of listeners who use streaming services would likely be more varied than those of listeners who do not use streaming services.
music publishers who choose to forgo releasing music on physical media are likely to see no change in revenue.
listeners who use streaming services would be more likely to give physical copies of music as gifts to others than to purchase physical copies for themselves.
listeners who prefer to purchase compact discs rather than use a service such as YouTube Music or Jango would tend to listen to older music.
questions.explanation: If each new song costs money under ownership but is free with streaming, streamers have no cost barrier to trying more kinds of music, so their listening should be more varied.

questions.passage: Some plants produce chemicals that repel plant-eating insects, but only after insects have started to damage them. In an experiment, researchers found that undamaged tomato plants growing near damaged ones also began producing more of these chemicals, even though nothing had touched them. Because the plants' roots were kept separate, the researchers suspect that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: the undamaged plants were reacting to insects that the researchers failed to notice.
the undamaged plants detected compounds released into the air by the damaged plants.
the damaged plants stopped producing repellent chemicals once their neighbors began.
tomato plants produce repellent chemicals only when they are grown in crowded conditions.
questions.explanation: The undamaged plants weren't touched and weren't connected by roots, so the signal most likely traveled through the air. A contradicts the statement that nothing had touched them.
